key_insight: Natural-image pretraining improved medical diffusion image generation, with benefits linked to spatial structure rather than semantic knowledge.
clinical_relevance: More faithful synthetic medical images could support research, but improved pathology-classification and radiomic metrics do not establish clinical utility or safety.
method: Compared natural-image initialization with training from scratch, medical pretraining, and reinitialization schemes.
Evaluated pixel- and latent-space diffusion models spanning 131M–952M parameters.
Probed semantic and spatial representations and tested mixed natural–medical image training.
evidence_signal: Across RadImageNet and BraTS, natural-image initialization improved relative gFID by 21–34% in pixel space and 14% in latent space; a spatial-structure metric tracked gFID with |r| = 0.85.
watch_item: Results cover two datasets and rely on proxy fidelity measures; broader generalization and clinical validity remain unproven.
paper_title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
